chapter_title: The Seventh, concerning the Five Fathers
chapter_note: Core layer dominates the middle: a structured, numbered emanation/evocation schema (five fathers; repeated triads of powers) with impersonal cosmological exposition. The chapter is wrapped in a hagiographic opening (¶1) and ends with a beatitude-style closure (¶23). Strong second-half institutional drift: explicit church/elect/catechumens material (¶13, ¶17–19, ¶21, and likely the paraenetic blessing ¶23) reflects later compilation/pastoral extension; NT/Gospel overlay appears in ¶15 (Jn 8-like saying) and the soteriological Gospel-toned phrasing in ¶10.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic hagiographic scene-setting: ‘Once again… apostle… disciples… revelation’ — classic Kephalaia frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Five fathers exist; they were summoned forth one of one. [Also], one did come out of another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered cosmological schema announced in impersonal expository voice; no citation or institutional tags.

paragraphs.core_text: The first Father is the Father of Greatness, the blessed one of glory, the [on]e who has no measure to his greatness; who also is the first only-begotten, the first eternal; who exists with fiv[e fa]thers for ever; the one who exists before every thing that has existed, and that will exist.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic divine taxonomy with Persian-Manichaean theonyms; definitional, non-parenetic exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Now he, the glorious Father, summoned from him three emanations. The [fi]rst is the Gre[at] Spirit, the first Mother, who came out of the Father. She appeared first. ⟨p.35⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation mechanics (‘summoned… three emanations’) in structured sequence; manuscript marker preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The seco[nd i]s the Belo[ved of] the Lights, the great glorious Beloved, [the one w]ho is honour[ed; w]ho came out of the Father. [He ma]nifested ou[t of h]im.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues ordered emanation list; purely cosmological naming and procession.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father is the Thir[d Ambassador], the eldest of [a]]] the counsell[ors; who came out of] the first Father. He appeared.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Emanation/appearance formula; Persian-Manichaean divinity in systematic role list.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first Father, the first power, the one from whom the three great powers came out. This is the first Father, the first eternal, the root of all the lights; from whom the three emanations came out. They have humiliated the Darkness. They have brought its heart's desire to naught. They have given themselves the victory. They have also given the victory to their aeons.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological conflict mechanics (Light vs personified Darkness) plus triadic emanations; impersonal declarative style.

paragraphs.core_text: The second father, who came out of the first Father, is the Third Ambassador, the model of the King of lights. And again, he too summoned and sent out of him three powers.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Iterative pattern (‘And again… three powers’) typical of older schematizing instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: One is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man; the one who bears up under all things; the great Pillar of blessing; the great porter, who is greater than all the porters.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic hypostasis described functionally (support/bearing); no ecclesial application.

paragraphs.core_text: The second is glorious Jesus the Splendour; [the] one through whom shall be given life eternal.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Jesus the Splendour appears here as a named cosmological entity in the triad list; the ‘life eternal’ phrasing is somewhat Gospel-toned, but not a citation or NT narrative and functions as cosmological soteriology.

paragraphs.core_text: The third is the Virgin of Light, the glorious wisd[o]m; the one who takes away the heart of the [rul]ers and the powers by her image, as she fulfils the pleas[u]re of the greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological agency (rulers/powers subdued by image) in systematic listing.

paragraphs.core_text: The third father, who came out of the second father: he is glorious Jesus the Splendour. And, again, he too summoned three evocations after the pattern of the second father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the iterative triadic structure (‘after the pattern…’), characteristic of core schemata.
Institutional graft: ‘father of all the apostles… churches… holy church… appointed’ applies cosmic language to ecclesial offices; this is not the older impersonal cosmological register.

paragraphs.core_text: The second power whom Jesus summo[n]ed is the gre[at Jud]ge, who gives judgement on all the souls of mankind, [his] dwelling being established in the atmosphere under [ ... / ... ] wheel [ ... ] stars.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to cosmological geography (atmosphere, wheel, stars) and functional office (Judge of souls) without church-institution markers.
Direct NT/Gospel entry: embedded dominical-style quotation (‘what I have seen with my Father…’) aligned with the chapter’s noted Jn 8 footnote; even if adapted, its vector is Gospel tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth father is the Light Mind, the one who chooses all the churches. And, again, he too summoned three powers after the pattern of Jesus.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the numbered father/triad schema; however ‘chooses all the churches’ is a mild institutional coloration—kept as core because it remains a definitional line inside the emanation list and not an editorial seam into rules/offices.
Ecclesial office and community-history language (‘Apostle of Light… assume the church of the flesh… inner leader’) reads as institutional role construction rather than cosmological mechanics.
Companion/assistant to the apostle with practical protection motifs; tied to apostolic office rather than cosmic structure.
Seam-flagged institutional extension: elect/catechumens and renunciation admonition; editor extends the triad pattern into church categories.

paragraphs.core_text: And also the fifth father is this Light Form; the one who shall appear to everyone who will go out from his body, corresponding to the pattern of the image to the apostle; and the thr[ee] great glorious angels who are come with her.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological/cosmological apparition on leaving the body plus triadic angelic accompaniment; ‘corresponding… to the apostle’ may be secondary coloration but the paragraph’s main substance is mythic/eschatological description.
Seam-flagged institutional extension: angelic items listed, then explicitly redirected ‘to the elect and the catechumens’—a classic editorial graft onto a cosmological list.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the five fathers who have come out of one another. They have appeared and man[ifes]ted through one another!
paragraphs.temporal_note: Schematic closure of the five-father chain; summary cadence typical of core list endings.
Beatitude/praise-style concluding exhortation (‘Blessed is he…’) with ethical titles (‘doers of good things’) functions as editorial closure rather than schematic cosmology.
